exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Domain of a Transformed Reciprocal Function

question.text: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=\dfrac{7}{3x-12}\,?$
question.explanation:
A reciprocal function is defined for all values of $x$ except for those that make the denominator zero. So, to find the domain, we must exclude all values of $x$ that make the denominator zero.

Setting the denominator equal to zero and solving, we get \begin{align*} 3x-12&=0\\[5pt] 3x&=12\\[5pt] x&= \dfrac{12}{3}\\[5pt] x&= 4. \end{align*}

Therefore, the domain is $x \in \left(-\infty, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4}\right)\cup\left( \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\infty}\right).$

question.text: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=-\dfrac{3}{4x-2}?$
question.explanation:
A reciprocal function is defined for all values of $x$ except for those that make the denominator zero. So, to find the domain, we must exclude all values of $x$ that make the denominator zero.

Setting the denominator equal to zero and solving, we get

\begin{align*} 4x-2&=0\\[5pt] 4x&=2\\[5pt] x&= \dfrac{2}{4}\\[5pt] x&= \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the domain is $x \in \left(-\infty,\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\cup\left(\dfrac{1}{2},\infty\right).$

A reciprocal function is defined for all values of $x$ except for those that make the denominator zero. So, to find the domain, we must exclude all values that make the denominator zero.

Setting the denominator equal to zero and solving, we get

\begin{align*} kx+4 &= 0\\[5pt] kx & = -4\\[5pt] x & = -\dfrac{4}{k}. \end{align*}

So, the point that must be excluded from the domain is $x = -\dfrac{4}{k}.$

On the other hand, we can see that $x=-\dfrac 1 2$ is excluded from the domain. Equating this to $-\dfrac 4k,$ we get

\begin{align*} -\dfrac{4}{k} & = -\dfrac{1}{2}\\[5pt] \dfrac{4}{k} & = \dfrac{1}{2}\\[5pt] k & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{8}. \end{align*}

Setting the denominator equal to zero and solving, we get

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Reciprocal Function

question.text: What is the range of the function $f(x)=-\dfrac{9}{2x+9} + 5\,?$
question.explanation:
A transformed reciprocal function of the form \[ f(x) = \dfrac{a}{bx+c} + d \] has the horizontal asymptote $y=d,$ and therefore, its range is \[ f(x) \in (-\infty, d)\cup (d,\infty). \]

In our case, $d = 5.$ Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is $y = 5,$ and the range of the function is \[ f(x)\in \left(\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\infty}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{5}\right) \cup \left(\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{5}, \infty\right). \]
